001: Was your trip to Germany only for work, or did you manage to enjoy it a little?
Unfortunately, it was all very rushed, but on the last day I took a walk around the historic center.
What a shame it was so tight. Did you at least get to try the local food?
Yes, that I did! I had dinner at a typical restaurant and tried a dish I had never seen in my life.
How cool! I would love to travel to Europe, but I haven't had that opportunity yet.
It's really worth it, but the ideal is to go with more free time to truly enjoy it.
002: Have you already decided where you're going for your mid-year vacation?
I'm still torn between the beach and the mountains, but I think I'll end up choosing the mountains.
Good choice! Cold weather goes well with a good wine and a fireplace.
Exactly what I was thinking. And you, do you already have plans or are you staying around here?
I'm going to travel to the Northeast with my family, we need to rest a bit.
Great destination! Just don't forget to bring sunscreen, the sun there is very strong.
003: How was the meeting with the investors in São Paulo?
It was productive, but the traffic and the heat of the city ended up wearing me out quite a bit.
I can imagine! Working outside the city always has those unexpected issues, doesn't it?
Yeah, but the result was worth it. We closed the partnership we were hoping for.
What great news! That deserves a celebration when you get back.
For sure! I'm going to schedule a dinner with the team to celebrate this achievement.
004: Do you usually extend your business trips to explore the city?
Whenever the schedule allows, I try to stay at least one extra day on my own.
That's a great strategy for balancing work and leisure.
I agree. I've already gotten to know amazing places that way, without needing to take entire vacations.
I should adopt that habit, but I always rush back home.
You should try it at least once, the experience completely changes the trip.
005: Do you prefer traveling by plane or by car on your vacations?
It depends on the destination. For farther places, the plane is unavoidable, but I love a road trip.
I like it too, mainly because we can stop wherever we feel like it.
Exactly! And the trip ends up becoming part of the fun, not just the final destination.
But with fuel prices, you have to plan the route well.
True, but with good planning you can enjoy it without spending a fortune.
006: Have you ever thought about turning your vacation into an opportunity to learn something new?
Actually, yes. I'm thinking about taking a cooking course in Italy.
Wow, what a fantastic idea! Combining travel and learning is the best of both worlds.
Yeah, I think I'll take advantage of being there and enroll in a local school.
And have you thought about how you'll balance the classes with sightseeing?
I'll leave the mornings for the course and the afternoons to explore the city at a relaxed pace.
007: How do you deal with jet lag when you travel for work?
In the beginning it was hard, but I learned to adapt already during the flight.
What technique do you use? I suffer a lot with that on my trips.
I already set my watch to the destination's time and try to sleep according to the local schedule.
Interesting! I'll try that on my next trip to Japan.
I also recommend avoiding coffee in the first few hours, that helped me a lot.
008: Do you think you can enjoy a vacation trip well with just one week?
You can, as long as you plan the route well and don't try to see everything at once.
I have the flaw of wanting to visit every possible tourist attraction.
I used to be like that too, but I ended up learning that less is more on a trip.
That makes sense. I'd rather come back from a place wanting to see more than feeling exhausted.
Exactly! And you still have that desire to go back, which is great for local tourism.
009: Have you ever had to cancel a business trip because of an unexpected event?
Yes, I have, and it was quite frustrating, especially because the event was important for the company.
And how did you handle the situation back then?
I had to reorganize my whole schedule and attend the meeting via video conference.
At least technology helped solve the problem, didn't it?
It did, but I admit it's not the same as being there in person.
010: Do you prefer traveling alone or with company on your vacations?
I've done both, but I admit I prefer traveling with company.
Me too! I think the trip is more fun when you have someone to share it with.
No doubt, but traveling alone also has its charm and teaches us a lot.
True, especially about independence and self-awareness.
Yeah, the important thing is to enjoy every moment, regardless of the company.
